newsitem.title: USA: Woman kills death row inmate at Arizona prison.
newsitem.headline: Woman kills death row inmate at Arizona prison.

text.p: A woman shot and apparently killed a death row inmate at a state prison Wednesday and was then shot to death herself by prison guards, authorities said.

Authorities said Floyd Bennett Thornton Jr., 36, was believed to have been killed by the female civilian at 7:52 a.m. PDT as he was tending a vegetable garden with other death row inmates outside a prison cell block.
The woman, firing from outside the prison fence, was shot in the legs and chest by prison guards, said state Department of Corrections spokeswoman Camilla Strongin.
The assailant was pronounced dead at the scene. Thornton died while being taken to a local hospital.
Local prosecutors said they believed that the woman, who has not been publicily identified, was Thornton's wife, although prison officials would not confirm that.
Authorities added that they not sure what prompted the incident near the prison complex in Florence, Ariz., about 60 miles southeast of Phoenix.

Witnesses reported that the woman drove up to the fence surrounding the prison grounds near state Highway 89 and opened fire from her car with a rifle. She then approached the fence began firing at Thornton with a handgun as he worked in a prison vegetable garden.

Thornton is said to have approached the woman and was knocked to the ground by a barrage of bean bag and rubber ball fire from prison guards. He got to his feet and was apparently killed by the woman, Strongin said.
"That's what we think happened at this point, but we can't be sure until the autopsy is in," she told Reuters.
Strongin said prison guards killed the woman after repeated attempts to get her to drop the weapon.

Thornton was on death row for the September 1993 murder of 74-year-old Dale Duke near Bisbee, Ariz. Thornton killed the man in front of his wife after escaping from a local jail where he was being held on second-degree murder charges.
He was sentenced to die for the Duke murder in January 1995.
